clue.text: Coast road is my special place

parts.note: cor! is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
a niche is a place specially suited to someone

explanation.surface: Someone declares a coastal drive their favourite spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is not possessive here but the exclamation, as in 'my, how lovely!'
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coast, famously on the Riviera.

clue.text: Get lost, not entirely unscathed

indicators.note: only part of the following word is used, so the letters sit inside it

parts.note: letters two to five of this word

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go away while not quite escaping harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is an informal command telling someone to leave at once, like 'go away'.

clue.text: Senior academic receives pay mainly to get rid of faculty

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped
a word that receives something takes it inside itself

parts.note: a dean heads a university faculty
a fee is a payment; mainly drops its last letter

explanation.surface: A senior professor takes a payoff to wind up a university department.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'faculty' is a university department; the definition's faculty is the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To deafen is to destroy someone's hearing, and hearing is one of the bodily faculties or senses.

clue.text: Evidence of settlement upset man in rainforest on vacation

indicators.note: one piece placed in another is put inside it
a word on vacation has emptied out, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters only

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a chessman is also called a piece

explanation.surface: A man overturned in a deserted rainforest somehow proves a deal was settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chess piece, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the written proof that a bill has been paid or settled.

clue.text: Discharge Democrat kicked out of blue state

indicators.note: something kicked out is removed from the larger word

parts.note: feeling blue is a state of low spirits
standard abbreviation for a Democrat

explanation.surface: A Democrat is thrown out of a Democratic-voting US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue state' reads as an American Democrat-voting state, but it is the mood of being blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejection and discharge both mean the act of throwing or sending something out.

clue.text: In contact with board about article up for discussion

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer words go round the small one

parts.note: on, as touching a surface
a board can be a table, as in 'bed and board'
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone talks to the company board about an article that is being debated.
explanation.walkthrough: The article sits between the two halves rather than inside one word: 'In contact with board' gives an outer pair split around it. 'board' here is a table, as in bed and board.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal on the table has been put forward and is open for discussion.

clue.text: In favour of accepting pound sterling in old money

indicators.note: a word accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: for, as in 'all those for?'
L, from libra, is the symbol for pound sterling
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone backs taking sterling in pre-decimal currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a British coin worth two shillings, used before decimalisation in 1971.

clue.text: Material that's used in construction

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the building material made of cement and aggregate

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description of a building material; 'Material' is also an adjective meaning solid and real.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete as an adjective means tangible or real, and as a noun it is the familiar building mix of cement, sand and stone.

clue.text: Psychiatrist barely escaped highly competitive environment

parts.note: Carl Jung, the Swiss psychiatrist

indicators.note: something bare is stripped, so the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: fled, stripped of its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist only just got out of a cut-throat workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' seems to mean 'only just', but it strips fled (escaped) bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a place a jungle is the idiom for a ruthless, every-man-for-himself setting.

clue.text: Draw together writer's material over time

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: what a writer puts on paper
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An author slowly gathers up their material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' suggests the yarn of knitting, but it is the writer's ink.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to draw together, as in knitting one's brows or a bone knitting as it heals.

clue.text: Something in the wind from Europe projecting growth in Jersey?

parts.note: French, from France in Europe
a horn grows out of a cow's head, and a Jersey is a breed of cow

explanation.surface: A rumour from the Continent about something sticking out on a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' is a breed of dairy cow, not the island; 'in the wind' means the wind section of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The French horn is a brass instrument played in the wind section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Dissident group ousting leader in fratricidal gesture

indicators.note: ousting throws something out, so one letter is removed

parts.note: a breakaway group within a larger body

indicators.note: 'leader in' keeps only the first letter of 'fratricidal'

parts.note: first letter of that word

explanation.surface: A rebel group gets rid of its head in a brother-killing move.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture can be any act or deed, as in 'a gesture of goodwill'.

clue.text: On-going support mainly blocking means of access

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped
something blocking a passage sits inside it

parts.note: ingress is a way in
a prop supports; mainly drops its last letter

explanation.surface: Continuing backing that mostly obstructs an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Work in progress is still under way, which is exactly what ongoing means.

clue.text: Suffering can start to generate work

parts.note: pain is suffering
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Hardship may be what gets a person working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting is a work of art, so work stands for it as a general term.

clue.text: Realise messenger's leaked material

parts.note: to see is to realise or understand
a page carries messages; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone realises a courier has passed on secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaked material' suggests secret documents but means liquid that has oozed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the fluid that has slowly escaped through a gap or porous surface.

clue.text: Catching sight of good way to deal with matter?

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a boil full of pus, or matter, is treated by piercing it

explanation.surface: Seeing a good method of handling some business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter' is used in its medical sense of pus.
explanation.definitionFit: Glancing at something is getting a brief look at it, so it is catching sight of it.

clue.text: Nosey creature is unable to stand missing start of conversation

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is left out

parts.note: can't bear means cannot tolerate

indicators.note: 'start of' keeps only the first letter of 'conversation'

parts.note: first letter of that word

explanation.surface: A busybody can't stand a chat that begins without them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nosey' suggests prying but is literal: the creature has a long snout.
explanation.definitionFit: The antbear, or aardvark, is an African mammal with a long snout for eating ants and termites.

clue.text: Reacting badly on almost being choked by fresh garlic

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
something choked by another is gripped inside it
fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
on is the leg side in cricket; almost drops the G

explanation.surface: Someone nearly gags on fresh garlic and has a bad reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so 'on' gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allergic means one's body reacts badly to a substance.

clue.text: Swimmer left in swimming pool couldn't know to begin with

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely and settle in a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
letters to be rearranged with L

indicators.note: what each word begins with is its opening letter

parts.note: first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A swimmer left in the pool didn't know how to start.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollock is a sea fish of the cod family, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Difficulty following depression as an alternative state

indicators.note: following places one piece after the others

parts.note: a col is a dip between two peaks
or introduces an alternative
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble after a bout of depression offers another state of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' reads as a state of mind; it is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Skilful plan eliminating staff work

indicators.note: eliminating gets rid of something, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a clever move or scheme
to staff is to man

explanation.surface: A clever scheme to cut jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Oeuvre is a French borrowing for an artist's body of work, or a single work.

clue.text: Bug in live telecast

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live

indicators.note: cast can mean thrown, so the letters before it are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the word splits as tele plus cast; tele supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A glitch appears during a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The word telecast splits into tele and cast, the second half working on the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect, and bug is the everyday word for one.

clue.text: Person who gets shot by outlaw carrying gun?

indicators.note: a word carrying another holds it inside

parts.note: to outlaw is to ban
a gun is a firearm, an arm

explanation.surface: A victim gunned down by an armed bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' reads as gunfire, but it is a small measure of spirits poured and served.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman serves drinks, so he is the one who gets you a shot of whisky.

clue.text: University starts to require registration in crucial changes relating to course

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the rearranged word
changes means the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A university needs enrolment during critical changes to its course.
explanation.definitionFit: Curricular describes anything belonging to a curriculum, the content of a course of study.

clue.text: Lived with learner losing items regularly

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: dropping every other letter at even intervals keeps the rest

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Shared a home with a student who keeps losing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Were is a past form of be, and to be is to exist or live, so it fits lived.

clue.text: Ladies' man disheartened female author

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the central letter

parts.note: Virginia Woolf, the novelist

explanation.surface: A womaniser has upset a woman writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf is slang for a predatory womaniser who chases women.

clue.text: Almost willing to accept one's captive here

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
accepting something takes it in

parts.note: prone means inclined or willing; almost drops the E
I is one, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly ready to admit they are being held.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison is the place where a captive is held, so it is where one is captive.

clue.text: Remained behind fellow minister

indicators.note: behind places the first piece after the second

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
lain, past participle of lie, as in stayed put

explanation.surface: A man stayed behind after a clergyman left.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a minister of religion attached to a college, hospital, regiment or prison.
